claims.claim: A fixed membrane and fixed fully accounted heat-per-charge coefficient imply Qdot <= integral_A(alpha^2/R_A) * (1/COP - deltaT/Tc), including optimized nonuniform currents and time scheduling.
assumptions: Closed cyclic heat pump between two reservoirs
All ionic strokes and duty counted in alpha
Joule dissipation at or below the hot reservoir temperature
No material or chemistry improvement hidden as a geometry improvement

claims.claim: Reported high-efficiency ionocaloric current density is approximately 5 A/m2; organic membrane resistance is reported approximately 100 times a typical aqueous value.
An illustrative 1 V useful-heat-per-total-charge coefficient at 5 A/m2 yields 5 W/m2 and 200 m2/kW before adverse duty or auxiliary losses.
Nanoconfined liquid transport ribs can defeat the demonstrated organic membrane limitation without changing membrane material or buying more area.
Capacitive or Faradaic salt extraction is an original ionocaloric escape invented in this branch.
Distributed shallow diaphragm, peristaltic, electrostatic, or liquid-piston compression constitutes a distinct conversion mechanism established in this branch.

An internally thermodynamically consistent approximate water-cycle envelope at 10-to-35 C requires 48.8 L/s hot-preheated suction flow per kW and ideal COP 10.97; 5 Hz/10 mm stroke requires 0.975 m2 active area, with 75.5 W additional-loss budget at COP 6.
The water-model exergy identity is satisfied to floating-point precision and its modeled COP remains below Carnot at the evaluated point.
A physically credible original transformative energy capability has been established.
